summary: Whitehead Point light: a brick tower lit in 1826, rebuilt after the 1846 hurricane, automated in 1915, now a museum where visitors can climb 88 steps.

structures.note: Present tower; archive gives 1847 as the year established. Raised 5 ft in 1872 and 20 ft in 1894-95 (LHF; Light-House Board reports).
Keepers' quarters, West Indian vernacular style (USLHS).

access.note: Museum open daily 10:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., last admission 4:30 p.m.; 88 steps to the top of the tower (KWAHS).

facts.agency: Key West Art & Historical Society (manages the site for Monroe County, the owner)

events.note: Brick conical tower, 65 ft to the base of the lantern, 15 whale-oil lamps; the archive gives 1825 as the year established.
Michael Mabrity first lit the lamps on 13 January 1826 (LHF).
Barbara Mabrity became head keeper after Michael's death.

October 1846 hurricane swept away the first tower and its keeper's house; press reports disagree: 14 persons died at the light (Richmond Enquirer first passage; New Orleans Bulletin letter), 15 at the Key West light (Richmond Enquirer later passage).
New tower completed 15 January 1848 at a cost of $7,247.77 (LHF); KWAHS says it opened in 1848.
Third-order Fresnel lens placed in the tower (LHF).
Tower raised five feet with a new lantern room (LHF). Wikipedia-style sources give 1873 for this change; LHF is used here.
Present keepers' dwelling completed (LHF; archive year 1887).
Third-order light taken out of service on 30 November 1894 while the tower was raised 20 ft.
Regular light reestablished 5 February 1895 (LHB 1895; LHF gives the same day); the contract work was recorded as completed 8 February 1895 (LHB 1895).
Keeper William Bethel fell from the dwelling roof while clearing gutters before a hurricane (LHF).
Incandescent oil vapor replaced by acetylene; light changed from fixed to occulting.
Keeper's constant care no longer required; soon automated (LHF).
Coast Guard took control of the lighthouse (LHF).
Key West Art and Historical Society granted control of the dwelling (LHF).
Coast Guard decommissioned the light; full-time keeper no longer needed (KWAHS; LHF).
Keepers' dwelling opened as a lighthouse museum (LHF).

corrections.why: LHF says the new tower was completed by 15 January 1848 and that the wooden keepers' dwelling was completed in 1849; KWAHS says the current lighthouse opened in 1848. The record's 1849 first_lit appears to match the dwelling year, not the light.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The archive gives 1825 as the year the station was established (a tower completed, not the first lighting). LHF gives 13 January 1826 for the first lighting, which is the date used here.

The archive gives 1847 for the present tower; LHF gives completion by 15 January 1848; KWAHS says it opened in 1848. Completion date 1848 is used. The archive's 1847 may be the year the rebuilding was funded or begun (LHF says work began in November 1847); this is a guess, not stated by any source.
The archive's 1847 'original lens installed' refers to the original optic of Argand lamps and reflectors. LHF dates the third-order Fresnel lens to 1858.
The archive span is 1832-1864 (32 years). LHF says she was appointed assistant in 1826 and counts 38 years of service at her dismissal. Both are reported in the text.

resolved_conflicts.field: keeper Mary E. Bethel end date
resolved_conflicts.explanation: The archive ends her head-keeper term in 1914; LHF says 1915. Both are reported in the text.
LHF gives 1872 for the five-foot extension; another summary gives 1873. Story uses 1872 and attributes it to LHF.

The archive records the station as discontinued in 1915, when the lamp was converted to acetylene and automated. The light was decommissioned by the Coast Guard in 1969 (KWAHS). Both dates are kept, with different meanings.

The Richmond Enquirer of 3 November 1846 gives 14 persons perished at the southwest-point light in one passage and 15 lost at the Key West light in another passage of the same issue; the reprinted New Orleans Bulletin letter gives 14. The story states both figures and does not pick one.

The LHB 1895 report gives the regular light reestablished on 5 February 1895 and the contract work completed 8 February 1895; LHF gives 5 February for the third-order light's return. The story gives the order as the sources state it.

notes_for_editor: Rich station with 12 sources. Keepers roster: all 23 lines are copied from the USLHS place record (roster.py), with person slugs; LHF's keeper list matches. Corpus LHB pages were located by scan page from the OCR index; printed page numbers are not confirmed (the page-number '?' flag is set on all of them), so check the scan before printing a page number. The Richmond Enquirer OCR is garbled around the keeper's house passage, so the story does not claim the keeper's house was destroyed by quotation; the storm's destruction of the light is quoted. Points resting on LHF alone (no primary source read): the 1847 appropriation and 1848 completion, the 1858 lens, the 1872 lantern raise, the 1887 dwelling date (USLHS agrees), the 1907-1908 storms and Bethel's death, the 1917 Demeritt request, the 1939 Coast Guard takeover, the 1966 KWAHS takeover, and the 1987 and 1990 dates. The 1913 Bulletin's William W. Demeritt and LHF's William Demeritt are presented separately; the sources do not say outright they are the same man. Barbara Mabrity's 1843 petition is quoted through LHF. The Coast Guard article on Barbara Mabrity (mycg.uscg.mil) returned HTTP 403 and was not read. Wikipedia was used for leads only and is not cited. The hmdb marker and the Keeper's Quarters museum ticket page were not used. The 1846 storm date (10 October) comes from LHF; the newspapers do not give a date for the storm itself. The 2016 renovation mentioned in Wikipedia was not verified and is left out. Fact-check 2026-10-28: Richmond Enquirer (3 Nov 1846) gives 14 and, in another passage, 15 deaths; the story states both. The LHB 1895 report puts the regular light's return (5 Feb 1895) before the work's completion (8 Feb 1895); the story says so. Mabrity's salary raise is LHF's suggestion, not the Treasury's. The Bulletin's William W. Demeritt (1913) is not identified with LHF's William Demeritt. The Demeritt 1913 and 1915 Bulletin quotations, the 1892 and 1894 Board quotations, and the Barbara Mabrity birth and death years were read directly from the sources.
